messages:
jen_support: FYI customer 'FinApps' reported a subtle language change after the recent model bump. They say replies are more hedged and add extra qualifiers like 'might', 'could', 'possibly' — fewer direct recommendations. They attached prompt + before/after outputs. Can ML + infra triage? :eyes:

jen_support: Customer example (copied):
> Prompt: \"Summarize the new loan policy and recommend next actions for compliance team.\"
> Response (redwood-model-2026-rc0): \"Summary: X. Recommendation: 1) update procedure A, 2) notify team B. Rationale: ...\"
> Response (redwood-model-2026-rc1): \"It might be reasonable to consider updating procedure A. You could also possibly notify team B, though you may want to verify with legal.\"

deploy-bot: rollout complete: redwood-model-2026-rc1 -> canary 20% at 2026-03-16T14:05:12Z :white_check_mark:

raj_ml: thanks — can you paste request_id(s), sampling params (temp/top_p), system prompt, and whether the customer pinned model or relied on default? Also any edit to post-processing or response filters?

jen_support: attaching customer log snippet and one request id: req_8f3a9b2c. They used our hosted API, default model param (no pin). Sampling: temp=0.2, top_p=0.95 per the customer's SDK logs. No custom post-processing on their side.

jen_support: API call they did:
```
POST /v1/generate
{"model": "redwood-model-2026", "request_id": "req_8f3a9b2c", "temp": 0.2, "top_p": 0.95, "prompt": "Summarize the new loan policy and recommend next actions for compliance team."}
```

emily_eng: Could a new safety or liability detector be injecting hedging language? Any chance the system prompt changed in the canary to add cautious phrasing?

mike_sre: Checked infra logs for req_8f3a9b2c — no errors, latencies normal. Traffic shows ~20% routed to rc1 at that time. No additional middleware modifications detected.

raj_ml: I ran a quick local repro with rc0 vs rc1 using the same prompt and sampling params. I can reproduce the increased qualifier tokens. Looking at the model config, rc1 introduced a small calibration tweak to the final token scoring (added a certainty penalty to reduce overconfident assertions). That penalty can nudge outputs toward hedging words.

raj_ml: short plan: 1) run A/B with and without the certainty_penalty flag to confirm impact, 2) if confirmed, either revert the penalty in canary or adjust magnitude, 3) push a targeted prompt tweak (post-processing rewrite rules) for affected customers if immediate revert isn't possible.

jen_support: Customer wants an ETA and asks we avoid churn. Any quick mitigation we can do while you validate?

raj_ml: Immediate mitigation: rollback canary to previous model build for that customer cohort (we can do targeted routing). I'll coordinate with deploy team. For a code fix, I expect a config patch today and a new canary by tomorrow morning if tests pass.

deploy-bot: rollback triggered: routing for accounts tagged \"finapps\" -> redwood-model-2026-rc0 (canary revert) at 2026-03-16T20:40:03Z.

jen_support: Thanks — I'll tell the customer we've routed them back to previous model and we'll follow up with a technical postmortem and timeline. :thumbsup:

raj_ml: I'll post the A/B diffs and token-level example callbacks in this thread once available. For now, blocking change is the certainty_penalty in scoring; toggling it reproduces/avoids the hedging behavior in my local tests.

mike_sre: FYI no infra impact; just saw the routing change applied successfully.

jen_support: Great. I'll close the customer loop and ask them to confirm whether the language feels back to normal. Thanks all.
